The most widely accepted measurement of this towering giant's apex—the point known scientifically as Summit I—is 8,848.86 meters above mean sea level at the Nepal-China border crossing.

However, it is worth noting that there are debates and differing opinions on exactly how high Mt. Everest reaches due to various factors such as snow accumulation changing over time or varying measurements techniques (e.g., GPS versus traditional triangulation).
